title: 7-round AES-128 impossible-differential key recovery, improved Bahrak-Aref construction

target.description: 7 rounds of standard AES-128 with initial AddRoundKey and final MixColumns omitted. The source reports complete master-key recovery, using impossible-differential subkey elimination followed by key-schedule completion or trial encryption.

setting.key_relation: One fixed unknown AES master key; no related-key oracle.
setting.key_population: general secret key; no weak-key restriction reported
setting.plaintext_model: source-reported chosen-plaintext budget for the improved Bahrak-Aref construction; Appendix B defers detailed structure and candidate-pair generation to the full online version
assumptions: Uses the four-round impossible differential of Proposition 1 with input/output extension and early rejection of wrong key guesses.
The appendix summarizes improvements to the Bahrak-Aref attack and describes efficient completion by guessing the last three bytes. The full online version is still pending.

preprocessing.note: Appendix B does not itemize this endpoint's preprocessing. The separate Appendix A elimination-table construction is not automatically assigned to the condensed Bahrak-Aref variant.

success.description: The acquired21-page full manuscript supplies the previously delegated seven-round AES128 BA procedure and matches its exact headline data/time. No numerical finite-budget complete-key success is supplied. Four related elimination runs share96 key bits and source data, then aggregate suggestions and perform residual completion; expected survivors and modeled fixed-wrong-guess survival are not actual-key recovery probabilities. The2^-13.25 single-run source survival model is retained only at2^112.2 data.Original resource units and unreported coordinates remain unchanged. A newly available procedure is not a new full-paper/forward audit.

review.scope: Targeted success re-audit with separately hashed independent-mirror supplementary edition. Exact endpoint budgets and output conditions checked; no new full-paper/forward completion or historic official-byte equivalence.

components.description: PDF6 Proposition1 and the source elimination rule: a true hypothesis cannot satisfy both conditions of the impossible differential and is not discarded by that mathematical contradiction. This is a local retention relation, not a finite-budget uniqueness or residual-search success rate.

Section4.1 Step2: eight zero ciphertext-difference bytes give source-model fraction2^-64. At AES128 data2^112.2 the source expects2^79.2 pairs; AES192/AES256 use their own2^113.8 budget. This is a pair filter, not a whole-key event.

Section4.1 AES128 aggregation: three explicit schedule relations supply a24-bit wrong-assignment filter before residual24-bit search. This component is only stored for AES128 and is not borrowed for the stronger AES192/AES256 filtering.

Section4.1: source single-run survival model, printed approximately2^-13.25, for one fixed wrong32-bit initial-column guess at the2^112.2 budget. The four overlapping runs are not multiplied into an independent whole-key success model.
